selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveler decide to do in order to gain a higher level of faith?
questions.answer: He decided to look at the whole universe and learn from what it shows.

questions.question: What tool did he use while examining the universe, and what does that suggest?
questions.answer: He used a kind of telescope taken from the Qur’an, which suggests he was viewing the world through guidance from revelation.

questions.question: How did the universe appear to him when he looked at it carefully?
questions.answer: It appeared full of meaning, well-arranged, and like a book, a palace, and a city made with purpose.

questions.question: What do the parts of the universe, like its sections and lines, point to?
questions.answer: They point to the existence and nearness of One Creator who knows everything and has power over everything.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the universe to a book?
questions.answer: Because its parts are connected, meaningful, and arranged in a way that shows planning and authorship.

questions.question: What do the constant changes in the universe help prove?
questions.answer: They help show that the One managing it is active, wise, and fully aware of all things.

questions.question: Besides the “book” example, what else in the universe gives testimony?
questions.answer: Its species, tiny particles, inhabitants, contents, and all the things entering, leaving, and changing in it also give testimony.

questions.question: What qualities of the Maker are shown by the changes and renewal in the cosmos?
questions.answer: They show unlimited power, endless wisdom, and unmatched skill.

questions.question: What two beliefs are clearly supported by the witness of the cosmos in this passage?
questions.answer: The existence of Allah and His oneness.

questions.question: What is the best overall conclusion from this passage?
questions.answer: The universe is a united sign that leads a person to believe in Allah’s existence and oneness.

questions.question: What was the traveler hoping to improve by studying the whole cosmos?
questions.answer: He wanted to strengthen and brighten his faith.

questions.question: Why did he turn from individual parts to the whole universe?
questions.answer: He wanted to gain a further level of belief by seeing the bigger picture.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the Qur’an help him do?
questions.answer: It helps him understand how to read the universe correctly.

questions.question: What are the three main images used to describe the universe?
questions.answer: It is described like a book, a decorated palace, and an orderly city.

questions.question: What do these images have in common?
questions.answer: All of them suggest design, order, purpose, and a maker behind them.

questions.question: What do even the smallest features of the universe show?
questions.answer: They show meaningful arrangement and point to a Creator who sees and knows all things.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Creator’s knowledge?
questions.answer: It describes Him as knowing each thing and also how everything is related to everything else.

questions.question: Which parts of the cosmos are said to speak with one voice?
questions.answer: Its kinds of creatures, tiny particles, residents, contents, and all its movements and changes speak together.

questions.question: According to the passage, what central message does the cosmos deliver?
questions.answer: It declares the existence and unity of one exalted Creator.

questions.question: If a student asked for the main lesson of this passage, what would be a good answer?
questions.answer: The main lesson is that the whole universe is like a clear sign leading us to know Allah exists and is One.

questions.question: What first step does the traveler take in this passage?
questions.answer: He encourages himself to move forward and seek another degree of faith.

questions.question: What does “listening” to the cosmos mean here?
questions.answer: It means paying attention to the signs and meanings found in creation.

questions.question: How does the passage present the universe as something readable?
questions.answer: It presents the universe as if it were written and structured like a text.

questions.question: Why is calling the cosmos a “book” an important comparison?
questions.answer: Because a real book has an author, so the comparison points to a deliberate Creator.
